title: The launch was the product
lede: Pepsi treated the introduction as an event: a teaser on inauguration eve, the Super Bowl, a rock anthem, buses wrapped in vinyl and an ice rink. The spending is known only from press estimates.

blocks.title: “Right Now”
blocks.body:
The commercials borrowed the block-letter captions of Van Halen’s video for “Right Now” as well as the song.[^22] Eddie Van Halen told Guitar World in 1996 that the band agreed because Pepsi would otherwise have re-recorded the song with studio musicians: “The only reason we gave Pepsi the music was because they were going to use the song anyway.”[^22]

The slogan was “You’ve never seen a taste like this.”[^12] It promised a new taste and showed a new look, and the gap between the two became the product’s problem.
blocks.caption: Six buses in San Francisco and Oakland were covered from headlights to taillights, windows included.[^13] Original illustration.

blocks.title: Nostalgia as the second campaign
blocks.body: The revivals were marketed on the 1990s, not on the drink. In 2016 PepsiCo released “The Crystal Pepsi Trail,” an online game styled after 1990s computer games.[^27][^31] In 2017 it ran a three-city Throwback Tour at baseball stadiums with Busta Rhymes, Mark McGrath and Salt-N-Pepa.[^32] In 2022 the price of entry was a photograph of yourself in the 1990s.[^34]
